steps.text: Conduction is how heat travels through a solid — from the hot end to the cold end. Let's watch it happen.
Tap “Start” to heat one end of the rod. Pins are stuck along it with wax.
The pins drop one by one — the one nearest the flame first, then the next. That order shows heat moving along the rod.
Heat always flows from hot to cold through the material. That's conduction, and it works best in metals.

coach.mission: Watch heat conduct along a rod and drop the pins in order.
whenStuck: Tap “Start” to heat the rod and watch the pins.
whenWrong: Heat moves from the hot end to the cold end, so the nearest pin drops first.
The order of the pins shows the direction heat travels.
whenCorrect: Right — the pins fall in order as heat conducts along the rod.
Good — heat flows from hot to cold through the metal.
coach.done: You've seen heat conduct through a solid. Reset and try again, or move on when you're ready.
